places.name: Kakum National Park
places.where: Central Region · 33 km north of Cape Coast
places.imageAlt: Rope canopy walkway strung between trees above the rainforest at Kakum
about: Kakum protects one of the last stretches of undisturbed rainforest in southern Ghana, covering roughly 375 square kilometres of the Central Region. The park is best known for its canopy walkway, a series of rope bridges suspended between hardwood trees and crossed on foot around thirty metres above the forest floor.

Below the canopy the forest supports forest elephants, bongo antelope, several primate species and over two hundred kinds of bird. Most visitors come for the walkway and the guided ground trails, both of which start from the visitor centre at the park entrance near Abrafo.

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: Tro-tro or taxi from Cape Coast, roughly 45 minutes

facts.label: Canopy walk
facts.value: Seven bridges, about 40 minutes end to end

facts.label: Guides
facts.value: Compulsory on all trails, arranged at the visitor centre

facts.label: Best time
facts.value: Early morning, before the tour groups arrive

facts.label: Bring
facts.value: Closed shoes, water, insect repellent

facts.label: Nearby
facts.value: Often combined with Cape Coast and Elmina in one day

places.name: Cape Coast Castle
places.where: Central Region · Cape Coast · UNESCO World Heritage Site
places.imageAlt: White stone walls of Cape Coast Castle facing the sea
about: Cape Coast Castle began as a Swedish trading post in 1653 and passed through Danish and Dutch hands before the British took it in 1664 and made it the headquarters of their administration on the Gold Coast. For nearly two centuries it was one of the largest holding sites in the transatlantic slave trade.

The tour moves between the airy governor's quarters above and the dungeons below, ending at the Door of No Return that opens onto the shore. It is a difficult visit and deliberately so. A museum on the upper floor covers Akan history and the wider trade.

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: Central Cape Coast, walkable from most of the town

facts.label: Tours
facts.value: Guided only, departing on the hour

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: About 90 minutes

facts.label: Museum
facts.value: Included, on the upper floor

facts.label: Note
facts.value: The dungeon section is confined and emotionally heavy

facts.label: Nearby
facts.value: Elmina Castle is 13 km west along the coast road

places.name: Elmina Castle
places.where: Central Region · Elmina · UNESCO World Heritage Site
places.imageAlt: Elmina Castle seen across the harbour
about: Built by the Portuguese in 1482 as São Jorge da Mina, Elmina is the oldest surviving European building in sub-Saharan Africa. The Dutch captured it in 1637 and held it for over two centuries before ceding it to the British in 1872.

The whitewashed fort sits directly above a working fishing harbour, and the contrast between the two is part of the visit. Tours cover the courtyards, the church the Dutch built inside the walls, and the dungeons beneath.

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: 13 km west of Cape Coast, about 25 minutes by taxi

facts.label: Tours
facts.value: Guided only, departing regularly through the day

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: About 75 minutes

facts.label: Harbour
facts.value: The fishing port below is busiest in the early morning

facts.label: Note
facts.value: Steep stairs and low doorways throughout

facts.label: Nearby
facts.value: Cape Coast Castle and Kakum both make an easy same-day pairing

places.name: Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park
places.where: Greater Accra · Central Accra · mausoleum and museum
places.imageAlt: Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park in Accra
about: The park stands on the old polo grounds where Kwame Nkrumah declared Ghana's independence in March 1957. It now holds the mausoleum of Ghana's first president and his wife Fathia, set behind a long avenue of fountains.

A museum below the monument covers Nkrumah's life, his role in pan-Africanism, and the 1966 coup that removed him. Personal effects, photographs and correspondence are on display, alongside the original statue toppled during the coup.

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: Central Accra, near the Independence Arch

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: About an hour including the museum

facts.label: Guides
facts.value: Available at the entrance, worth taking

facts.label: Photography
facts.value: Permitted in the grounds

facts.label: Best time
facts.value: Late afternoon, when the heat drops

facts.label: Nearby
facts.value: Independence Square and the National Museum are both close

places.name: Mole National Park
places.where: Savannah Region · Near Damongo · Ghana's largest national park
places.imageAlt: Elephants at a waterhole in Mole National Park
about: Mole covers roughly 4,577 square kilometres of guinea savannah in northern Ghana, making it by far the country's largest protected area. Elephants are the draw, and they are regularly seen at the waterholes below the escarpment where the park accommodation sits.

Unusually, Mole allows walking safaris with an armed ranger as well as vehicle drives. Buffalo, warthog, kob, roan antelope and several primate species are common; the park also records over three hundred bird species.

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: About two hours by road from Tamale to Damongo

facts.label: Safaris
facts.value: Walking and vehicle drives, both ranger-led

facts.label: Best time
facts.value: Dry season, roughly November to April, when animals gather at water

facts.label: Timing
facts.value: Drives leave at dawn and late afternoon

facts.label: Stay
facts.value: Book accommodation inside the park well ahead

facts.label: Bring
facts.value: Neutral clothing, binoculars, sun protection

places.name: Aburi Botanical Gardens
places.where: Eastern Region · Akuapem Hills · 30 km north of Accra
places.imageAlt: Terraced lawns and mature trees at Aburi Botanical Gardens
about: Opened in 1890 on the site of a former sanatorium, Aburi covers around 64 hectares of the Akuapem ridge. The avenue of royal palms at the entrance is the best-known feature, but the collection runs to hundreds of species across the terraces.

The hills sit several hundred metres above Accra and are noticeably cooler, which is most of the reason city residents come up at weekends. Craft stalls line the road into town, and the drive up through Peduase is worth the trip on its own.

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: About an hour from Accra by road, longer in traffic

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: Two hours is comfortable

facts.label: Terrain
facts.value: Gentle slopes and paved paths

facts.label: Best time
facts.value: Weekday mornings, when it is quiet

facts.label: Nearby
facts.value: Woodcarving stalls along the Aburi road

facts.label: Bring
facts.value: A light layer — it is cooler than Accra

places.name: Wli Waterfalls
places.where: Volta Region · Agumatsa Reserve · near Hohoe
places.imageAlt: Water falling down a cliff face into a pool at Wli
about: Wli is the highest waterfall in Ghana and among the highest in West Africa, dropping in stages down a cliff on the Togo border. The lower falls are reached by a level 45-minute walk through the Agumatsa reserve, crossing the river several times on footbridges.

The upper falls take a much harder climb of two to three hours up the escarpment, and reward it with a view over both countries. Thousands of fruit bats roost on the cliff face above the lower pool, and the sound carries a long way.

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: About 20 km from Hohoe, then a short drive to the reserve gate

facts.label: Lower falls
facts.value: 45 minutes each way, mostly flat

facts.label: Upper falls
facts.value: Two to three hours each way, steep and unshaded in places

facts.label: Guides
facts.value: Compulsory, arranged at the gate

facts.label: Swimming
facts.value: Allowed in the lower pool

facts.label: Best time
facts.value: Rainy season for volume, dry season for the trail

places.name: Shai Hills Resource Reserve
places.where: Greater Accra · Near Doryumu · 50 km from Accra
places.imageAlt: Rock outcrops rising from grassland at Shai Hills
about: Shai Hills is the closest wildlife reserve to Accra, a stretch of grassland and inselbergs covering around 51 square kilometres. Olive baboons are everywhere and unbothered by visitors; kob, bushbuck and introduced zebra are also present.

The hills themselves hold caves once occupied by the Shai people before their removal in 1892, and several are open to visitors with a guide. The rock outcrops are climbable and give a long view across the Accra plains.

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: About 90 minutes from central Accra on the Akosombo road

facts.label: Activities
facts.value: Game drives, cave visits, rock climbing, birdwatching

facts.label: Guides
facts.value: Required for the caves and hills

facts.label: Baboons
facts.value: Keep food out of sight — they will take it

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: Half a day is enough

facts.label: Best time
facts.value: Early morning for wildlife

places.name: Labadi Beach
places.where: Greater Accra · La, Accra · also called La Pleasure Beach
places.imageAlt: Wide sand beach with palms at Labadi
about: Labadi is the busiest beach in Ghana and the most reliably lively stretch of the Accra coast. Weekends bring live highlife and reggae bands, drumming groups, horse riding along the sand and a steady run of food stalls behind the beach.

It is a social beach rather than a quiet one. The surf has a strong undertow and swimming is best kept close to shore. Several hotels along the strip maintain their own sections with loungers and calmer crowds.

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: About 20 minutes east of central Accra

facts.label: Entry
facts.value: A gate fee applies, higher at weekends

facts.label: Weekends
facts.value: Live music from the afternoon onwards

facts.label: Swimming
facts.value: Strong undertow — stay near the shore

facts.label: Food
facts.value: Grilled tilapia and kelewele from the stalls behind the sand

facts.label: Best time
facts.value: Sunday afternoon for atmosphere, weekday morning for quiet

places.name: Mount Afadjato
places.where: Volta Region · Liati Wote · the highest peak in Ghana
places.imageAlt: Mount Afadjato rising above the treeline
about: Mount Afadja, usually called Afadjato, rises to about 885 metres on the Ghana–Togo border and is the highest point in the country. The climb starts from the village of Liati Wote, where the community runs the trail and provides guides.

It is steep rather than long — most people reach the summit in 90 minutes to two hours. The last section is a scramble through scrub. On a clear morning the view runs across the Volta hills and well into Togo.

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: From Hohoe to Liati Wote, then the trail starts in the village

facts.label: Climb
facts.value: 90 minutes to two hours up, about an hour down

facts.label: Difficulty
facts.value: Steep and unshaded in places — take more water than you think

facts.label: Guides
facts.value: Arranged in the village, fees support the community

facts.label: Best time
facts.value: Start at first light, before the heat

facts.label: Nearby
facts.value: Tagbo Falls is a short walk from the same village

places.name: Lake Volta
places.where: Volta Region · Akosombo and north · the world's largest reservoir by area
places.imageAlt: Boats on the water at Lake Volta
about: Lake Volta was created by the Akosombo Dam in 1965 and covers around 8,500 square kilometres, making it the largest man-made reservoir in the world by surface area. It stretches north from Akosombo through much of eastern Ghana.

Most visitors experience it from the Akosombo end, where boat cruises run on the lower lake and the dam itself can be viewed from the overlook. A passenger ferry also runs the length of the lake to Yeji, a long journey through country few tourists see.

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: Akosombo is about two hours from Accra by road

facts.label: Cruises
facts.value: Day and sunset boats run from the Akosombo jetty

facts.label: Ferry
facts.value: A long-haul service runs north to Yeji

facts.label: Dam
facts.value: Viewable from the overlook; access is restricted

facts.label: Best time
facts.value: Late afternoon, for the light on the water

facts.label: Nearby
facts.value: Boti Falls and the Akosombo hotels

places.name: Kintampo Waterfalls
places.where: Bono East Region · 4 km north of Kintampo
places.imageAlt: Water spilling over rock steps into a pool at Kintampo Waterfalls
about: Kintampo Waterfalls is a chain of cascades on the Pumpum River, a tributary of the Black Volta, set in forest just outside Kintampo town. The water drops in stages, the largest about 25 metres, for a total fall of roughly 70 metres. In colonial times it was known as Sanders Falls, and it has been a tourist site since 1992.

The site closed after a storm in 2017 brought a tree down on visitors, and reopened in 2019 with new safety work and a canopy walkway. It sits right on the Kumasi to Tamale highway, which makes it the natural rest stop on any road trip north.

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: On the Kumasi to Tamale road, a short taxi ride from Kintampo

facts.label: Steps
facts.value: The lowest fall is 173 steps down and 151 back up

facts.label: Canopy walk
facts.value: Added when the site reopened in 2019

facts.label: Best time
facts.value: May to October for volume, November to March for clearer water

facts.label: Swimming
facts.value: Allowed in the lower pool when the guides say it is safe

facts.label: Nearby
facts.value: Boabeng-Fiema Monkey Sanctuary is about an hour south

places.name: Lake Bosomtwe
places.where: Ashanti Region · 30 km southeast of Kumasi
places.imageAlt: Lake Bosomtwe ringed by forested crater walls
about: Lake Bosomtwe is Ghana's only natural lake, filling a meteorite crater about 10.5 kilometres across that formed roughly a million years ago. The lake covers around 49 square kilometres, reaches 81 metres at its deepest, and has no river flowing out of it.

About thirty villages sit around the shore. The Asante regard the lake as sacred, and fishermen traditionally paddle out lying on wooden planks rather than in boats. Abono is the main village for visitors, with guesthouses, canoe trips and walks along the crater rim.

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: About 45 minutes from Kumasi by road to Abono

facts.label: Activities
facts.value: Canoe rides, swimming, crater-rim hikes, cycling round the lake

facts.label: Tradition
facts.value: Fishing from padua planks instead of boats

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: A day trip, or an overnight to see sunrise on the water

facts.label: Best time
facts.value: Dry season, roughly November to March

facts.label: Nearby
facts.value: Manhyia Palace in Kumasi on the way back

places.name: Manhyia Palace Museum
places.where: Ashanti Region · Kumasi · seat of the Asantehene
places.imageAlt: The white colonial-era building of the Manhyia Palace Museum in Kumasi
about: Manhyia is the seat of the Asantehene, king of the Asante. The British put up the original building in 1925, after destroying the earlier palace, and it served as the royal residence until a new palace was built beside it.

The old palace opened as a museum in August 1995. Inside are royal furniture, a bronze head of Prempeh II, an early map of the Asante kingdom and life-sized wax figures of past kings and queens, with statues of former rulers in the courtyard.

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: Northern Kumasi, a short taxi ride from the centre

facts.label: Tours
facts.value: Guided, through the old palace rooms

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: About an hour

facts.label: Photography
facts.value: Usually restricted inside — ask at the desk

facts.label: Festivals
facts.value: Akwasidae ceremonies at the palace follow the Akan calendar

facts.label: Nearby
facts.value: Kejetia Market and Lake Bosomtwe

places.name: Boabeng-Fiema Monkey Sanctuary
places.where: Bono East Region · near Nkoranza
places.imageAlt: A monkey in the trees at Boabeng-Fiema
about: Boabeng and Fiema are two neighbouring villages that share a 4.4 square kilometre patch of forest with around 700 monkeys, mostly Campbell's mona and black-and-white colobus. People here have treated the monkeys as sacred for generations.

Hunting them is forbidden, and when a monkey dies it is given a funeral and buried in its own cemetery. The monkeys move freely through the villages, and guided walks take you into the forest where the colobus troops live.

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: From Nkoranza by taxi, or off the Kintampo road

facts.label: Guides
facts.value: Arranged at the visitor centre

facts.label: Rule
facts.value: Do not feed the monkeys

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: One to two hours

facts.label: Best time
facts.value: Early morning, when the troops are most active

facts.label: Nearby
facts.value: Kintampo Waterfalls is about an hour north

places.name: Larabanga Mosque
places.where: Savannah Region · near the Mole park gate
places.imageAlt: The whitewashed mud walls and wooden spikes of Larabanga Mosque
about: Larabanga Mosque is a small Sudanese-style mosque of mud and timber, said to date from 1421, which makes it the oldest mosque in Ghana. It is sometimes called the Mecca of West Africa.

The building is only about eight metres square, braced by twelve buttresses with wooden beams sticking out of the walls. It was damaged by a storm in 2002 and restored with help from the World Monuments Fund.

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: 15 km north of Damongo, about 4 km from the Mole entrance

facts.label: Entry
facts.value: Non-Muslims view from outside; a local guide shows you round

facts.label: Dress
facts.value: Cover shoulders and knees

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: Under an hour

facts.label: Also see
facts.value: The Mystic Stone on the edge of the village

facts.label: Nearby
facts.value: Easy to pair with a safari at Mole

places.name: Paga Crocodile Pond
places.where: Upper East Region · Paga · on the Burkina Faso border
places.imageAlt: A crocodile resting on the bank of the pond at Paga
about: The Chief's Pond at Paga is home to crocodiles that the town considers sacred. Local belief holds that each crocodile is linked to a person in the community, so killing one is forbidden, and the legend behind this is several centuries old.
Because they have lived alongside people for so long, the crocodiles are unusually calm. Visitors buy a live chicken to feed them, and a guide will help you crouch beside one for a photograph.

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: About 40 km north of Bolgatanga by road

facts.label: Feeding
facts.value: Chickens are sold at the pond

facts.label: Safety
facts.value: Only approach with a guide

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: About an hour

facts.label: Nearby
facts.value: Pikworo Slave Camp, a short drive away

facts.label: Best time
facts.value: Morning or late afternoon, out of the midday heat

places.name: Nzulezo Stilt Village
places.where: Western Region · near Beyin · on Lake Tadane
places.imageAlt: Wooden houses on stilts above the water at Nzulezo
about: Nzulezo is a village built entirely on stilts and wooden platforms over Lake Tadane, home to more than 500 people. Houses, a school and a church all stand above the water, linked by a main boardwalk.
You reach it by dugout canoe, a trip of about an hour through reeds and raffia palms from Beyin. The village has been on UNESCO's tentative World Heritage list since 2000.

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: Canoe from Beyin, about 5 km and an hour each way

facts.label: Sacred day
facts.value: Thursday — the village does not receive visitors

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: Half a day including the canoe ride

facts.label: Bring
facts.value: Sun hat, water and something to keep your phone dry

facts.label: Fees
facts.value: Paid at the visitor centre in Beyin

facts.label: Nearby
facts.value: Fort Apollonia in Beyin

places.name: Akosombo Dam
places.where: Eastern Region · Akosombo · on the Volta River
places.imageAlt: Water released through the spillway of the Akosombo Dam
about: Akosombo Dam was built between 1961 and 1965 to power Ghana's aluminium industry. It is a rock-fill wall 660 metres long and 114 metres high, and it still supplies a large share of the country's electricity.
Damming the Volta created Lake Volta, the largest reservoir in the world by surface area. The project displaced about 80,000 people, a cost still remembered in the towns along the shore.

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: About two hours from Accra by road

facts.label: Tours
facts.value: Arranged through the Volta River Authority

facts.label: Photography
facts.value: Restricted at the dam itself — ask first

facts.label: Views
facts.value: The terrace of the Volta Hotel looks over the dam

facts.label: Combine with
facts.value: A cruise on Lake Volta from the Akosombo jetty

facts.label: Best time
facts.value: Late afternoon for the light

places.name: Tongo Hills and Tengzug Shrine
places.where: Upper East Region · south of Tongo
places.imageAlt: Granite boulders piled on the slopes of the Tongo Hills
about: The Tongo Hills are a range of granite outcrops south of Tongo, where huge boulders are stacked into strange shapes. In the dry season the wind across the rocks makes a whistling sound.
The hills hold the Tengzug shrines, which are deeply sacred to the people who live here. A guided walk takes you through the village, between the boulders and up to viewpoints over the savannah.

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: About 30 minutes from Bolgatanga by road

facts.label: Guides
facts.value: Arranged in Tengzug village

facts.label: Shrine visits
facts.value: Visitors remove their shirts as a sign of respect

facts.label: Terrain
facts.value: Rocky scrambles — wear proper shoes

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: Half a day

facts.label: Nearby
facts.value: Paga Crocodile Pond and the Bolgatanga basket market

places.name: Cape Three Points
places.where: Western Region · the southernmost point of Ghana
places.imageAlt: The old lighthouse on the headland at Cape Three Points
about: Cape Three Points is the southernmost tip of Ghana, a forested headland between the villages of Akwidaa and Princes Town. On a map it is said to be the land closest to where the equator meets the prime meridian.

The British built a lighthouse here in 1875 for ships crossing the Gulf of Guinea. Its ruins stand beside a taller lighthouse finished in 1925 that still works, and the coast on either side has some of the quietest beaches in the country.

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: From Takoradi via Agona Nkwanta; the last stretch is rough road

facts.label: Lighthouse
facts.value: The keeper may let you climb for a small tip

facts.label: Beaches
facts.value: Akwidaa and Cape Three Points village

facts.label: Swimming
facts.value: Currents can be strong — ask locally

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: A full day, or stay over at a beach lodge

facts.label: Nearby
facts.value: Busua and Fort Metal Cross at Dixcove

places.name: Ankasa Conservation Area
places.where: Western Region · near the Côte d'Ivoire border
places.imageAlt: A shining-blue kingfisher perched in the Ankasa forest
about: Ankasa covers about 500 square kilometres in the far southwest, joining Nini-Suhien National Park with the Ankasa Forest Reserve. It is the only protected area in Ghana inside the wet evergreen rainforest belt.

Forest elephants, bongo, leopards, chimpanzees and Diana monkeys live here, along with more than 800 plant species, over 600 kinds of butterfly and around 190 birds. Most visitors come to walk the trails and look for birds.

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: Off the Elubo road, west of Axim

facts.label: Guides
facts.value: Required on all trails

facts.label: Wildlife
facts.value: Birds and butterflies are easy; mammals are shy

facts.label: Bring
facts.value: Rain jacket, insect repellent, closed shoes

facts.label: Best time
facts.value: Dry season, roughly December to March

facts.label: Nearby
facts.value: Nzulezo Stilt Village

places.name: Tafi Atome Monkey Sanctuary
places.where: Volta Region · 43 km south of Hohoe
places.imageAlt: A mona monkey sitting on a branch at Tafi Atome
about: Tafi Atome is a community-run sanctuary set up in 1993 to protect the village's sacred grove. Its mona monkeys have long been seen locally as messengers of the gods.

Since the village stepped up protection in 1996 the monkey population has grown, and the forest's birds and butterflies have recovered with it. New visitor facilities opened in 2020, and fees go back into the community.

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: About 230 km from Accra; turn off between Ho and Hohoe

facts.label: Tours
facts.value: Guided walks into the grove

facts.label: Feeding
facts.value: Bananas are offered under the guide's direction

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: About an hour

facts.label: Best time
facts.value: Early morning or late afternoon

facts.label: Nearby
facts.value: Wli Waterfalls and Mount Afadjato

places.name: Jamestown Lighthouse
places.where: Greater Accra · Jamestown, old Accra
places.imageAlt: The red and white Jamestown Lighthouse above the rooftops of old Accra
about: The red and white lighthouse in Jamestown, the oldest part of Accra, has guided ships into the city since 1932. It stands on the site of an earlier light from 1871 and rises about 28 metres.

From the top you look over the fishing harbour, the colourful canoes and the old British fort. The lanes below are home to Ga fishing families, boxing gyms and murals painted for the Chale Wote street art festival.

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: Central Accra, at the end of High Street

facts.label: Climb
facts.value: A caretaker takes you up for a small fee

facts.label: Tours
facts.value: Local guides run walking tours of Jamestown

facts.label: Best time
facts.value: Late afternoon, when the boats come in

facts.label: Festival
facts.value: Chale Wote street art festival, usually in August

facts.label: Nearby
facts.value: Black Star Square and the Nkrumah Memorial Park

places.name: Black Star Square
places.where: Greater Accra · Independence Avenue, Accra
places.imageAlt: The Independence Arch and parade ground at Black Star Square
about: Black Star Square, also called Independence Square, was commissioned by Kwame Nkrumah and completed in 1961. Its stands seat around 30,000 people, making it one of the largest public squares in the world.
The square holds the Independence Arch and the Black Star Gate, whose star echoes the Black Star shipping line of Marcus Garvey. Ghana's Independence Day parade takes place here every 6 March.

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: Central Accra, on the seafront

facts.label: Entry
facts.value: Free to walk around outside events

facts.label: Events
facts.value: Independence Day parade on 6 March

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: 30 minutes to an hour

facts.label: Best time
facts.value: Early evening, when it cools down

facts.label: Nearby
facts.value: Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park is a short walk away

places.name: Ada Foah
places.where: Greater Accra · where the Volta meets the sea
places.imageAlt: Palm trees along the sandy beach at Ada Foah
about: Ada Foah is a coastal town at the mouth of the Volta River, known for the estuary islands and palm-lined sandbars where the river meets the Atlantic. Riverside chalets make it a favourite weekend escape from Accra.

Boats take you between the islands for swimming, fishing and sunset trips. The Danes built Fort Kongenstein here in 1783, and coastal erosion has left only part of it standing. The Asafotufiami festival is celebrated in the Ada area each August.

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: About two hours east of Accra by road

facts.label: Boats
facts.value: For hire at the riverside harbour

facts.label: Swimming
facts.value: Calmer on the river side than the ocean side

facts.label: Festival
facts.value: Asafotufiami, first week of August

facts.label: History
facts.value: Remains of Fort Kongenstein near the shore

facts.label: Best time
facts.value: Weekdays, when it is quieter

places.name: Fort William, Anomabu
places.where: Central Region · Anomabu · UNESCO World Heritage Site
places.imageAlt: The white walls of Fort William at Anomabu
about: Fort William was begun in 1753 by the British Company of Merchants, after they blocked a French attempt to build on the same spot. It was designed by John Apperly, its first governor, and completed by Richard Brew in 1760.

Like the castles at Cape Coast and Elmina, it was used in the Atlantic slave trade, and in 1979 it was added to UNESCO's World Heritage List with the other forts of the Ghana coast. It is quieter than the big castles and well preserved.

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: About 17 km east of Cape Coast on the coast road

facts.label: Tours
facts.value: Guided by the caretaker

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: About 45 minutes

facts.label: Note
facts.value: Holding cells are confined and dark

facts.label: Best time
facts.value: Morning, before the heat

facts.label: Nearby
facts.value: Cape Coast Castle and Kakum

places.name: Busua Beach
places.where: Western Region · 30 km west of Takoradi
places.imageAlt: Surfers riding waves off Busua Beach
about: Busua is a fishing village with a long sandy beach on the Gulf of Guinea. The water is calmer than most of Ghana's coast, and it has become the country's main spot for learning to surf.
Fishing for tuna and marlin still drives the village. A 25-minute walk west brings you to Dixcove and the old British Fort Metal Cross, and to the east is the Dutch Fort Batenstein.

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: Paved road from Takoradi, about 45 minutes

facts.label: Surfing
facts.value: Board hire and lessons on the beach

facts.label: Walks
facts.value: Dixcove and Fort Metal Cross, 25 minutes west

facts.label: Food
facts.value: Fresh fish and lobster at the beach shacks

places.name: Salaga Slave Market
places.where: Savannah Region · Salaga, East Gonja
places.imageAlt: One of the wells where captives were washed at Salaga
about: Salaga was the largest slave market in the region during the 18th and 19th centuries. Captives brought here were sold and then marched south to the coastal forts for export across the Atlantic.

The town was also a great trading centre for kola, and its mix of peoples earned it the name Timbuktu of the South. Today you can see the bathing site where captives were washed before sale, a baobab marking the old market and a small museum.

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: About three hours by road from Tamale

facts.label: Guides
facts.value: Arranged locally — they explain each site

facts.label: Sites
facts.value: Bathing site, market baobab and the slave museum

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: Two hours

facts.label: Note
facts.value: A sobering visit, best paired with Cape Coast

facts.label: Nearby

places.name: Boti Falls
places.where: Eastern Region · northeast of Koforidua
places.imageAlt: Twin waterfalls dropping into a forest pool at Boti
about: Boti Falls is a pair of waterfalls side by side, separated by a rocky ledge. Local tradition calls them male and female, the larger one being male, and says a rainbow appears when the two join in the rainy season.
The water falls about 30 metres into a pool where visitors swim. The falls sit at the bottom of around 250 concrete steps in the Huhunya forest, and guides lead walks on to nearby rock formations.

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: About 30 minutes from Koforidua, 90 minutes or more from Accra

facts.label: Steps
facts.value: About 250 down to the pool

facts.label: Entry
facts.value: Includes a guided tour and hike

facts.label: Best time
facts.value: June to August, when the falls merge

facts.label: Swimming
facts.value: Allowed in the pool

facts.label: Nearby

places.name: Gambaga Escarpment
places.where: North East Region · Gambaga and Nakpanduri
places.imageAlt: The long sandstone ridge of the Gambaga Escarpment over the plain
about: The Gambaga Escarpment is a sandstone ridge that runs for around 100 kilometres across northeastern Ghana, forming the raised northern edge of the Volta basin. It turns the White Volta west before the river bends south again.
Gambaga, once capital of the Mamprugu kingdom, sits beneath the cliffs. Nakpanduri, on top of the ridge, is the usual starting point for hikes, with wide views across the plains below.

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: From Tamale via Walewale to Gambaga

facts.label: Hiking
facts.value: Start from Nakpanduri for the best views

facts.label: Guides
facts.value: Ask in town — trails are not marked

facts.label: Best time
facts.value: Early morning in the dry season

facts.label: Bring
facts.value: Plenty of water and sun protection

facts.value: Nalerigu, seat of the Nayiri
